question: In vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF), the woman experiences continuous, uncontrollable leakage of urine that cannot be voluntarily stopped, distinguishing it from stress incontinence.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. VVF causes constant, uncontrollable urinary leakage through the vaginal opening — the fistulous tract bypasses the sphincter, so no voluntary control is possible. This distinguishes it clearly from stress incontinence, where involuntary loss occurs only with effort.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. VVF causes continuous involuntary urine loss through the vagina because urine bypasses the urethral sphincter entirely. The woman cannot store or control urine at all — this is the hallmark that distinguishes VVF from stress incontinence, where some voluntary control remains.
